s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of focal upper limb weakness
salient_findings: Sudden weakness of the left upper limb
Weakness of the distal phalanx of the thumb and middle phalanx of the index finger
Decreased grip strength on the left
key_facts: Episodes of isolated, sudden weakness of the left upper limb
Electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve
MRI of the left upper extremity showed no abnormalities

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of focal upper limb weakness
salient_findings: Sudden weakness of the left upper limb

Electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve

shortlist.label: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve

shortlist.label: Neuralgic Amyotrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of focal upper limb weakness without sensory deficits

shortlist.label: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of focal upper limb weakness with neurogenic atrophy

shortlist.label: Median Nerve Compression
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve

shortlist.label: Hirayama Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Focal upper limb weakness with neurogenic atrophy, particularly in young adults

raw.rationale: The electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve, which directly supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Neuralgic Amyotrophy
rejected.why: While it involves nerve damage, the specific involvement of the anterior interosseous nerve points more directly to Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome

rejected.label: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is more generalized and typically involves severe pain, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Median Nerve Compression
rejected.why: The symptoms and electromyographic findings are more specific to the anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve, rather than median nerve compression itself

rejected.label: Hirayama Disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with progressive muscular atrophy and is more common in young males, which does not match the patient's profile
